messages:
sasha: heads-up — new model bring-up (hf://org/llama-x-7b) failing our evals after conversion. quality regression on simple QA and weird tokenization around <|endoftext|>. looks like weights are misaligned across shards

sasha: error from load step: 
```
ERROR: Unexpected tensor shape for key model.layers.22.attn.k_proj.weight expected (1024,1024) got (512,1024)
WARNING: safetensors index lists shards in order: shard_0.safetensors, shard_1.safetensors, shard_2.safetensors
```

raj: can you paste the convert-tool + hf_hub version and the exact command you ran? also which rev was pinned?

sasha: converter v0.9.2, hf_hub 0.17.1, command: `redwood-hf-convert --from hf://org/llama-x-7b --to redwood --quantize int8 --emit-index` — no explicit --preserve-names flag. we used rev `v3.1` from the hub.

oliver: fwiw ive seen this pattern before when the safetensors index order doesn't match the weightname mapping step — converter renames keys using a stable map but then writes shards in a different order, and downstream loader assumes index==name-order. causes half the layers to pull the wrong slice.

maria: also noticed tokenizer config.json has `add_eos_token: false` in the HF repo, but our chat template assumes EOS present. could be compounding the eval regression (truncated prompts vs shifted positions).

ingest-bot: hub-downloader: fetched 3/3 shards (200 OK) for org/llama-x-7b@v3.1. index.json checksum ok. repo file list: [vocab.json, merges.txt, config.json, shard_0.safetensors, shard_1.safetensors, shard_2.safetensors]

sasha: repro steps: fresh checkout, `pip install redwood-convert==0.9.2`, run convert command above, then `redwood-run-eval --suite sanity-smoke --model converted/llama-x-7b`. results: EM down ~12%, and attention head outputs look scrambled in layer visualization.

raj: quick triage — can you run `python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; print(list(safe_open('shard_0.safetensors').keys())[:5])"` on each shard and paste key prefixes? want to confirm which keys live in which shard.

sasha: done. output:
```
shard_0: model.layers.0.*model_attn.*
shard_1: model.layers.12.*
shard_2: model.layers.24.*
```

oliver: aha — the rename map we generate assumes interleaved layer assignment (0,1,2..) but in this HF release the original packing used block-chunking (0..11 in shard_0, 12..23 in shard_1...). converter's packing->indexer step flipped ordering when writing the safetensors index, so loader thinks shard_0 contains early layers but index points to later layers.

maria: immediate mitigation: re-run converter with `--emit-index --preserve-shard-order` (internal flag) and validate key->shard mapping before pushing. also set `add_eos_token: true` in the local config.json or adjust our chatfmt fallback to tolerate missing EOS.

devops-bot: canary for dedicated GPUs failed for canary id canary-2024-07-22-03 — observed model mismatch assertion in runtime during start: `Layer checksum mismatch at layer 12` — rollout paused.

raj: i'll open a small PR to the converter: add a unit that cross-checks index.json order against actual safetensors key placement and errors out (or reorders index) if mismatch. will target master->0.9.x patch. assigning oliver to review.

oliver: sounds good. also propose adding a minimal integration test: produce a fake HF repo that writes shards with non-interleaved packing and ensure converter keeps correct mapping.

sasha: for now, workaround notes for infra:
- on the affected model, pin to converted artifact `converted/llama-x-7b@build-20240722-fix` that we produced with manual reorder
- update eval harness to include tokenizer edge-case (missing eos) so we catch chatfmt shifts earlier

maria: logging action items:
- raj: PR for index vs shard crosscheck (ETA 3h)
- oliver: review + integration test (ETA EOD)
- sasha: regenerate converted artifact and upload to staging (ETA 1h)
- infra: restart canary after artifact swap (devops team)

ingest-bot: note: recorded as incident/inc-2024-07-22-llama-x-convert in the tracker.

raj: quick question — do we want the converter to default to `--preserve-weight-names` or keep current behavior and fail fast? leaning fail-fast so we don't silently produce bad artifacts. thoughts?

oliver: fail-fast with clear error and a link to docs. silent renames have bitten us too many times. :+1:

sasha: agreed — fail-fast. i can add a brief snippet to the docs about tokenizer EOS and chatfmt expectations.

maria: thanks everyone — i'll coordinate the canary restart once sasha uploads the artifact. :rocket:
